clue.text: Cut a weed

definitions.meaning: to cut short, as with a tail or wages
a coarse broad-leaved plant of the sorrel family, common on waste ground

explanation.definitionFit: To dock is to trim or reduce, and dock is also a familiar wild plant whose leaves soothe nettle stings.

clue.text: Detective Sergeant without one taints and purifies

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the sergeant's letters go around the next piece

parts.note: DS is the standard police abbreviation for Detective Sergeant
the Roman numeral for one is I
to taint is to contaminate or infect

explanation.surface: A police sergeant who stays away from someone corrupts them, yet somehow cleans them too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it carries its old sense of outside: the sergeant's letters wrap around the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinfect a surface or wound is to cleanse it of germs, a kind of purification.

clue.text: Professorship for one in menial work

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the word for drudgery

parts.note: char is British for housework or cleaning work, done by a charwoman
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone reduced from a university post to scrubbing floors.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR, British for cleaning or household drudgery, takes I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A university chair is a professor's established post, so the word stands for a professorship.

clue.text: Specify writing with a small animal in private cabins

parts.note: to state something is to specify or set it down
roo is the shortened form of kangaroo, a small word for the animal
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Someone stipulates a manuscript plus a pet for the private quarters on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small' here is a hint that the animal word is a shortened form: ROO for kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Staterooms are the private sleeping cabins on a passenger ship or train.

clue.text: Crime in which treachery starts taking place over sense

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting one piece over another sets it above, so the letter comes first
the opening letter of the word treachery is what starts it

parts.note: reason is good sense or sound judgment

explanation.surface: A crime that begins with betrayal and outweighs good judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: The T from 'treachery starts' is placed over (above, in this down entry) REASON.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country, is one of the gravest offences in law.

clue.text: Canopies for triers

definitions.meaning: a tester is the canopy over a four-poster bed or a pulpit
people who try or test things out

explanation.definitionFit: A tester is both an old word for a bed canopy and someone who samples or checks something.

clue.text: Moving fast and quietly in foray

indicators.note: the soft letter is set inside the word for an attack

parts.note: a foray is a sudden raid into enemy territory
p (piano) is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A swift, silent incursion into enemy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: P, piano or quietly in music, goes inside RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means swift, describing something going at speed.

clue.text: Instrument is returned to the storage container

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Instrument is returned to the storage container' (9). ORGAN + IS gives ORGANIS, but the final ER can only come from 'returned' read as RE turned, so one word is both fodder and reversal indicator; no other word supplies ER.
annotationWithheld.clue: Instrument is returned to the storage container

clue.text: Utters "yes" in a steamship

indicators.note: the word of assent is placed inside the ship's abbreviation

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
ay or aye is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Someone agrees aboard a steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: The old form of yes survives in Parliament's 'the ayes have it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something is to speak or voice it aloud.

clue.text: Came to pass, it existed — about autumn

indicators.note: around: the word for existed surrounds the season

parts.note: it has been, so been stands for existed
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Something happened once, around the autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it existed' is unusual: read it as 'it has been', which supplies the past participle; 'autumn' uses the American word.
explanation.definitionFit: Befallen is the past participle of befall, to happen or occur, often to someone.

clue.text: Express a smaller quantity for those without nationhood

parts.note: to state something is to express it in words
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Saying something is in short supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Stateless people have no country recognising them as citizens.

clue.text: Eat ravenously on motor yacht, being an abnormally small person

parts.note: to pig or pig out is to eat greedily
MY is the abbreviation for motor yacht, as in ship names

explanation.surface: Someone gorging themselves aboard a motor yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: PIGMY is an older spelling of pygmy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigmy or pygmy is a person of unusually small stature.

clue.text: Duck in rain turned into means of raising water

indicators.note: turned means the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A duck sitting in the rain becomes a water pump.
explanation.walkthrough: O, the cricket duck (a score of nought), joins RAIN, and the five letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A noria is a water wheel fitted with buckets, used to lift water for irrigation.

clue.text: Going very fast, chant about retreating sea

indicators.note: around: the word for chant surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to chant is to sing

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word for the sea is read in reverse

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea

explanation.surface: A chant about the tide going out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea' as 'the deep' is a poetic convention; 'retreating' turns it round before 'about' sets it inside the chant word.
explanation.definitionFit: Speeding means driving or moving faster than allowed, at high velocity.

clue.text: Not spotted in river, so relaxed

indicators.note: the river letter goes inside the word for unmarked

parts.note: unstained means clean, without spots or marks

explanation.surface: A clean garment washed in the river, so all is calm.
explanation.walkthrough: R for river slips inside UNSTAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstrained means free of tension or effort, so easy and at ease.

clue.text: Formation for London district with a man left on

parts.note: EC is the postal district of East Central London
he is a male pronoun, standing for a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A formation for a London district where a man stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode area for the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a stepped formation of troops, ships or aircraft.

clue.text: Halter for horse with a man found guilty of treason

parts.note: a hack is a horse for ordinary riding
Sir Thomas More was convicted of treason under Henry VIII and beheaded

explanation.surface: A rope for a horse belonging to a convicted traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: MORE is Sir Thomas More, executed in 1535 for treason against Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackamore is a bitless bridle or halter used in breaking horses.

clue.text: Old actress who almost makes last performance

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a swan song is a final performance before retiring

explanation.surface: An old screen star whose farewell show nearly happens.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloria Swanson was a Hollywood star of the silent era and Sunset Boulevard.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria Swanson was a famous American film actress of the 1920s to 1950s.

clue.text: Times to declare estimations of mean

parts.note: to aver is to declare or assert
ages are long times or eras

explanation.surface: A newspaper about to declare its figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it simply means ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Averages are calculations of the mean value of a set of numbers.

clue.text: Study of art of sleuth hot on what is almost precise

parts.note: tec is short for detective, a sleuth
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: nice can mean precise or subtle, as in a nice distinction

explanation.surface: A detective, hot on the trail, studies art with near precision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nice' in its older sense of exact or subtle loses its final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Technic is an older form of technique, the study and method of an art or craft.

clue.text: Vehicle is held up by king. It is a primitive boat

indicators.note: the king's name holds the next piece within it

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A vehicle delayed by a monarch, while a little boat is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The king is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme; 'up' turns the vehicle in this down entry, and 'held' puts it inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round boat of wicker and hide, an ancient Welsh and Irish craft.

clue.text: An entertainer putting rubbish on the jetty

indicators.note: in an across entry, putting a piece on another puts it after

parts.note: a jetty is a pier
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A performer dumping refuse on the pier.
explanation.walkthrough: PIER then ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pierrot is a clown or entertainer in white costume, once a feature of seaside shows.

clue.text: Wanderer is forbidding after insolence arising

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first
in a down entry, rising means the word reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: lip is cheeky talk or insolence
grim means stern or forbidding

explanation.surface: A traveller turns stern after some cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: LIP read upwards is PIL, followed by GRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim journeys to a holy place, and the word extends to any wayfarer.

clue.text: Royal place makes something soothing before exam

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: balm is a soothing ointment
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A soothing ointment taken before a test.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is the British royal family's castle in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Balmoral Castle in Aberdeenshire is a residence of the British royal family.

clue.text: Relative to make sound of crow for bird

parts.note: ma is mother, a relative
a caw is the call of a crow

explanation.surface: A family member imitates a crow to get a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large brightly coloured parrot.

clue.text: Artist follows a turn in the market-place

indicators.note: the artist's letters come after the other pieces

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist follows a stroll in the market square.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the public square and market of an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: Star hunter

parts.note: a mythical Greek hunter set among the stars as a constellation

explanation.definitionFit: Orion was a giant huntsman of Greek myth, placed in the night sky as a prominent constellation.

clue.text: Prices soaring, this petrol provider admitted

indicators.note: the brand name is taken in by the words, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Fuel prices go up and a petrol company admits it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaring' suggests the letters read upwards, but they run forwards in priCES SOaring.
explanation.definitionFit: Esso is a well-known brand of petrol stations, owned by ExxonMobil.

clue.text: Philosopher thus holding the office, initially

indicators.note: the Latin word for thus contains the next letters

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

indicators.note: the first letters of the words are what is meant

explanation.surface: A philosopher who, just so, keeps hold of the job at first.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC holds T and O, the first letters of 'the office'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic was a follower of Zeno's school of philosophy, known for calm endurance.

clue.text: Gemstone Scotsman found by dog-wood

indicators.note: the Scotsman is placed beside the tree, after it

parts.note: the cornel is a dogwood shrub or tree
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scotsman finds a gem next to a dogwood tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornelian, or carnelian, is a reddish semi-precious variety of chalcedony.

clue.text: Finished, Gilbert holds the rudder and submerges

parts.note: over means ended or finished

indicators.note: Gilbert's initials hold the steering word inside them

parts.note: W S Gilbert wrote the words for the Gilbert and Sullivan comic operas
the helm is the steering gear, the rudder or tiller

explanation.surface: Gilbert, done with the opera, takes the helm and sinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert is the librettist of Gilbert and Sullivan, known by his initials; 'holds' sets the steering word inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwhelm is to bury or flood over, as water engulfs something.

clue.text: A girl could be back to eat

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: A girl might come back to have dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a girl's name, as in Enid Blyton.
